description: Iowa-only rules checked against the cited statutes and official DMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Iowa's statutory speed in a business district is
questions.explanation: Iowa Code section 321.285(2)(a)(1) makes 20 miles per hour the lawful speed in any business district, unless another provision applies or a different limit is posted under the sections listed in subsection 2.

questions.q: Iowa's statutory speed in a residence or school district is
questions.explanation: Section 321.285(2)(a)(2) sets 25 miles per hour in any residence or school district. Subsection 2(b) requires each school district, as defined in section 321.1(70), to be marked by distinctive signs from the adopted manual on uniform traffic control devices, placed at the limits of the school district.

questions.q: Iowa's statutory speed in a suburban district is
questions.explanation: Section 321.285(2)(a)(3) sets 45 miles per hour in any suburban district unless another provision of the section applies or a different limit is posted under the listed sections.

questions.q: Iowa's speed on the interstate road system, and on a fully controlled-access divided multilane highway that is not described as interstate, is
options: 65 on the interstate and 55 on other controlled-access highways
70 on the interstate and 65 on other controlled-access highways
60 on both because of Senate File 378
questions.explanation: Section 321.285(5)(a) sets 65 miles per hour for all vehicular traffic on fully controlled-access, divided, multilane highways, and 70 miles per hour on highways that are part of the interstate road system as defined in section 306.3.

questions.q: On an Iowa secondary road that is not surfaced with concrete or asphalt, the daytime and nighttime statutory limits are
questions.explanation: Section 321.285(4): on a secondary road, the limit is 55 mph between sunrise and sunset and 50 mph between sunset and sunrise. A secondary road surfaced with concrete or asphalt takes the subsection 3 limit instead, which 2026 Iowa Acts chapter 1132 (Senate File 378) raised from 55 to 60 mph.

questions.q: Iowa's operating-while-intoxicated alcohol concentration is
questions.explanation: Iowa Code section 321J.2(1)(b) says a person commits OWI while having an alcohol concentration of .08 or more. Subsection (1)(a) separately covers being under the influence of an alcoholic beverage or other drug or a combination.

questions.q: A person under 21 in Iowa shall not operate a motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of
options: Any alcohol only if a passenger is under 18
questions.explanation: Section 321J.2A(1) says a person under twenty-one shall not operate a motor vehicle while having an alcohol concentration of .02 or more. The department revokes the license or nonresident operating privilege for the period in section 321J.12. That revocation does not prevent a criminal prosecution, but an OWI revocation under section 321J.2 supersedes it.

questions.q: For an Iowa under-21 revocation, the alcohol concentration of a specimen withdrawn within two hours after driving is
options: Presumed to be the level when driving
Used only if a blood test
Rounded down to the nearest tenth
questions.explanation: Section 321J.2A(2) states that presumption for a blood, breath, or urine specimen withdrawn within two hours after the defendant was driving or in physical control.

questions.q: A habitual offender under Iowa Code section 321.555(1) is a person with
questions.explanation: Section 321.555(1) lists offenses including manslaughter from operating a motor vehicle, OWI under section 321J.2, driving while the license is suspended, denied, revoked, or barred, and a felony under the motor-vehicle laws or a felony in which a motor vehicle is used. Three or more of the listed serious offenses, singularly or in combination, within a six-year period.

questions.q: Iowa may issue an instruction permit under section 321.180B to an applicant who is
questions.explanation: Section 321.180B(1) allows an instruction permit between the ages of fourteen and eighteen. A permittee under 18 must be accompanied by a parent, guardian, or custodian, an immediate family member at least 21, an approved driver-education instructor, or a person at least 25 with written permission, and that person must occupy the seat beside the driver.

questions.q: An Iowa intermediate licensee operating between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m. must be accompanied by a qualified supervising driver unless
options: A waiver covers school or work
The licensee is 16 and a half
A friend over 18 is on the phone
questions.explanation: Section 321.180B(2) states that 12:30 a.m. to 5:00 a.m. accompaniment rule and the waiver for school-related extracurricular activities and work. Unless a parent or guardian waives it when the license is issued, the first six months also limit unrelated minor passengers to one, except when the licensee is accompanied under subsection 1. Passengers are also limited to the number of passenger safety belts.

questions.q: In Iowa, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Iowa issues a learner's permit for a car at 14 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Iowa car permit: 14 years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321.180B Graduated driver’s licenses for persons aged fourteen through seventeen

questions.q: In Iowa, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Iowa requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 12 months.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321.180B Graduated driver’s licenses for persons aged fourteen through seventeen

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Iowa complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Iowa requires 20 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321.180B Graduated driver’s licenses for persons aged fourteen through seventeen

questions.q: Of a Iowa teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Iowa requires at least 2 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Iowa: 2 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321.180B Graduated driver’s licenses for persons aged fourteen through seventeen

questions.q: In Iowa, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Iowa, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321.180B Graduated driver’s licenses for persons aged fourteen through seventeen

questions.q: In Iowa, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Iowa drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 17 years.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321.180B Graduated driver’s licenses for persons aged fourteen through seventeen

questions.q: How many questions are on the Iowa car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Iowa car knowledge test has 25 questions.

provenance.manual: Iowa Driver's License Practice Test | Department of Transportation

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Iowa car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Iowa car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Iowa Driver's License Practice Test | Department of Transportation

questions.q: In Iowa, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Iowa, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.
questions.remember: Iowa, 21 and over: 0.08% is over the limit.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321J.2 Operating while under the influence of alcohol or a drug or while having an alcohol concentration of .08 or more (OWI)

questions.q: In Iowa, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Iowa sets the under-21 limit at 0.02%.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321J.2A Persons under the age of twenty-one

questions.q: In Iowa, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Iowa brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Iowa, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Iowa?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Iowa can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Iowa rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Iowa?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Iowa, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Iowa left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Iowa's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: Iowa seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321.445 Safety belts and safety harnesses — use required

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Iowa?
questions.explanation: Iowa requires a car seat or booster until 6 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Iowa: car or booster seat until 6 years.

questions.q: What is Iowa's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Iowa requires at least $20,000 / $40,000 / $15,000.

provenance.manual: Iowa Code §321A.21 “Motor vehicle liability policy” defined
